title: Roast Pork Belly
subtitle: Slow-roasted pork belly with crackling
excerpt: A thick slab of pork belly slow-roasted until the fat is completely rendered and the flesh is melting tender, then blasted at high heat for crackling so crisp it shatters.

recipe.sourceNotes: Roast pork belly is one of the most forgiving of all roasting joints: the high fat content makes it nearly impossible to overcook, and the slow render followed by a blast of high heat reliably produces good crackling. Pork belly is a fatty, layered cut from the underside of the pig. It was long considered an economical cut and only relatively recently became prized restaurant and home-cooking fare. The key to crackling is thorough drying of the skin and a very high final heat: moisture in the rind prevents it from puffing and crisping. Scoring the skin at close intervals allows the fat beneath to bubble up and the rind to blister. In East Asian cooking (particularly Chinese and Filipino) pork belly is the centrepiece of many celebration dishes; the Western approach of very slow roasting followed by a high-heat finish mirrors the technique used across cultures.

recipeTools.notes: A roasting tin large enough to hold the belly flat.

content.text: The single most important step is to dry the skin completely before roasting. Score the rind at 1 cm intervals with a sharp knife, then pat very dry and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight or for at least 2 hours. The drier the rind, the better the crackling. Rub the scored rind generously with fine salt, which draws out any remaining moisture. For the crackling blast at the end, watch the oven closely: it can go from perfect to burnt in minutes.

items.preparation: skin scored at 1 cm intervals, dried overnight uncovered in the fridge

content.text: Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Mix the fennel seeds, pepper, and a little salt. Rub the flesh side (not the skin) with the spice mix, garlic, and rosemary. Place skin-side up in a roasting tin. Rub the skin with the fine salt.
Roast for 2 hours until the flesh is very tender and shrinking from the sides. The skin will have started to blister but will not yet be fully crisped.

Increase the oven to 240 C / fan 220 C / gas 9. Return the belly for 20 to 25 minutes until the rind is deeply blistered and fully crisped. Watch carefully. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting through the crackling with a sharp knife or kitchen scissors.
